evidence.claim: In 1924, S. Davies Warfield brought an extension of the Seaboard Air Line Railroad through the community and planned its transformation into the line’s southern hub.
evidence.quote: Warfield planned to make Indiantown the southern hub of the Seaboard rail line.

evidence.claim: He laid out streets and built a school, housing and a station.
evidence.quote: laying out streets and building a school, housing, and a railroad station.

evidence.claim: He also built the Seminole Inn, which is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

evidence.claim: The land boom faded after 1926; Warfield’s death the next year ended the headquarters plan, and the 1928 hurricane halted further development.
evidence.quote: The Florida land boom of the 1920s fizzled out after 1926. Warfield died a year later, putting an end to plans to make Indiantown the Seaboard's southern headquarters. The 1928 Okeechobee hurricane wreaked significant destruction and halted further development.

evidence.claim: Passenger service ended in 1971, and the depot was later demolished.
